To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the majority of patients with rectal cancer will develop local or regional failure following surgery alone, and that these patients are likely to have a better prognosis with postoperative radiation than with surgery alone.

local and regional failures are common following “curative” resection for rectal cancer, that patterns of failure can be predicted by anatomical and initial pathologic factors, and that postoperative irradiation may improve local‐regional disease‐free survival.

the majority of patients who fail following curative resection of rectal cancer have local and/or regional failure, that this failure is often predictable based on preoperative staging, and that adjuvant therapy may be a logical treatment for these patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following: (1) The identification of factors which may be associated with an increased risk of local failure and/or regional failure.
the development of an effective adjuvant radiation program for the treatment of rectal cancer.
the following: (1) The development of an experimental animal model for the study of the effects of ionizing radiation and chemotherapeutic agents on the growth of human tumors implanted in nude mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LF‐RF is the predominant pattern of failure following curative surgery for rectal cancer and is not uncommon even when the initial operation was “curative” and the patient was “cured.”
the most frequent pattern of failure following curative surgery was local‐regional.
the incidence of local‐reginal recurrence is high, that it is predictable, that it is not related to distant metastases, and that it can be treated by irradiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most important factor in the development of failure is the initial pathologic stage of tumor.
the most common pattern of recurrence after “curative surgery for adenocarcnoma of the rectosigmoid is local‐regional.
patients with rectal adenocarcinomas that have invaded the bowel wall or have lymph nodes positive for tumor should be treated postoperatively with irradiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are a lot of failures in this group of patients, and they are mostly local and regional.
the majority of patients who develop a recurrence after curative intent surgery will develop a recurrence in the pelvis or regional nodes.
the majority of patients who develop recurrence after curative surgery have a failure pattern that can be explained by anatomical factors and the initial pathologic extent.
